decision_note: Collaea study quantifies pollinator and antagonist visitation and opposing selection on flower size/number with attacked versus non-attacked female fitness.

Six herbivore species induce species-specific floral changes with contrasting pollinator visitation responses.

bioRxiv preprint of Sasidharan et al. 2023; published Annals of Botany representation is SCHPRISMA-000339/source-registry anchor.
Frontiers study combines natural/simulated florivory, changed floral expression and hummingbird pollination; no antagonist response to do(A).

Evolution Letters experiment evolves defence/floral plasticity under factorial herbivory and pollination regimes.

Silene study links herbivory-induced VOCs to pollinator-attracting function and higher fruit set, including volatile addition.

Descriptive floral/pollination biology records nectar thieves but does not test one floral A against pollinator and antagonist responses.
Dissertation surveys floral biology/visitors across tree species; florivore mention does not resolve a focal antagonist response to the same floral coordinate.
Zieria breeding/pollination study includes seed predation context but does not link a declared floral attraction coordinate to both pollinator and antagonist responses.
Floral Evolution: Breeding Systems, Pollinators, and Beyond is a synthesis/review, retained for source chasing but excluded from independent primary-study counting.
Fifty-year floral-nectar synthesis is useful source-registry material but not an independent primary experiment.
Artificial-flower experiment shows nectar guides improve legitimate visits and discourage nectar robbing by bumblebees.
Floral phytochemistry article is a broad synthesis of volatile/nectar chemistry effects and is source-registry material rather than an independent primary report.
Whole-plant floral-scent perspective/review synthesizes pollinator and antagonist contexts; exclude from primary study count.
Terpenoid feeding trials directly test a facultative florivore, while pollinator attraction is prior/contextual evidence rather than a pollinator response measured in this study.

Chemodiversity study compares visitor groups including pollinators/florivores and plant fitness consequences; frozen preprint now has a final publication.
Cleistocactus study records hummingbird pollination, nectar robbery and reduced stigma pollen loads in robbed/damaged flowers.
